roles.title: Data QA Engineer
roles.overview: A Data QA Engineer makes sure the data that a business relies on is correct, complete and on time. They write SQL and automated checks that run against pipelines and tables, define what 'good data' means with data owners, and catch problems before dashboards, reports or downstream systems consume bad records.
responsibilities: Define data quality rules with data owners across completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, uniqueness and timeliness
Write SQL checks that validate row counts, null rates, key uniqueness, referential integrity and value ranges
Automate data tests so they run as part of pipeline execution and block or flag bad loads
Investigate data incidents, trace them to the source system or transformation step and document root cause
Design and maintain representative test datasets, including edge cases such as late-arriving records and duplicates
Review schema changes and transformation logic for downstream impact before they reach production
Report data quality trends to stakeholders in terms of affected tables, consumers and business impact

essential: Strong SQL: joins, aggregates, window functions and set operations
Data quality dimensions and how to turn each into a testable rule
Understanding of relational modelling, primary and foreign keys
Test design for data: boundaries, nulls, duplicates and invalid formats
roleSpecific: Automated data testing with a framework such as dbt tests or Great Expectations
Source-to-target reconciliation techniques
Reading pipeline orchestration logs, for example Apache Airflow task runs
optional: Python for scripted checks and data profiling

prerequisites: Comfort writing SELECT queries with joins and GROUP BY
Basic understanding of software testing concepts such as test cases and defects

beginner.title: SQL and data quality foundations
goals: Write queries that find nulls, duplicates and orphaned foreign keys in a sample schema
Explain the six common data quality dimensions with one example check for each
Profile a table: row count, distinct counts, min/max and null percentage per column
Log a data defect with the query, expected result and actual result

intermediate.title: Automated data checks in pipelines
goals: Implement uniqueness, not-null, accepted-values and relationship tests in a dbt or Great Expectations project
Build a source-to-target reconciliation on counts, sums and sampled row-level comparisons
Use window functions to detect gaps and duplicates in time-series data
Run data checks from a CI job and fail the build on violations

advanced.title: Data quality strategy and incident handling
goals: Classify tables by business criticality and set check depth and freshness targets accordingly
Run a root cause analysis for a data incident and propose a preventive check
Define data quality metrics and a reporting cadence for stakeholders
Review schema change proposals for downstream breakage

exercises: Given an orders and customers schema, write five queries that each expose a different data quality problem
Write dbt tests for a staging model: unique and not-null on the key, accepted values on status, relationship to customers
Reconcile a CSV source file against its loaded table and report count, sum and row-level differences
Detect duplicate events within a five-minute window using a window function

sampleProject.title: Data quality suite for an e-commerce orders pipeline
sampleProject.description: Load a public-domain or generated orders dataset into PostgreSQL, build a small dbt project with staging and mart models, and add tests for uniqueness, nulls, referential integrity, accepted values and freshness. Seed deliberate defects (duplicate order ids, negative totals, orphaned customer ids) and show the suite catching each one, with a short report of findings.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you turn the phrase 'the data must be accurate' into concrete tests?
interviewQuestions.a: I would break accuracy down with the data owner into checkable rules: values match a trusted source (reconcile against the source system on keys and sums), values fall within valid ranges (no negative quantities, dates not in the future), derived fields match their formula (line total equals quantity times unit price), and codes belong to a reference list. Each rule becomes an automated check with a threshold and an owner, and anything that cannot be checked automatically gets a sampled manual review.

interviewQuestions.q: A dashboard shows revenue 3% lower than finance expects. How do you investigate?
interviewQuestions.a: First I confirm both sides use the same definition: currency, tax inclusion, refunds, time zone and date cut-off. Then I reconcile layer by layer: source system totals for the period, staged data, transformed models and the dashboard query. The first layer where the totals diverge localises the problem. Typical causes are filtered-out records in a join (inner join dropping rows with missing dimension keys), duplicated rows from a many-to-many join, late-arriving data, or time-zone boundaries. I document the cause and add a check that would have caught it.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test that a join does not silently drop or duplicate rows?
interviewQuestions.a: Compare row counts before and after the join and against the expected grain. For a left join on a key that should be unique on the right side, the output count should equal the left count; if it is higher, the right key is not unique, so I test uniqueness on it. To find dropped rows, I run an anti-join (left join where right key is null) to list unmatched keys. I also check sums of an additive measure before and after.

interviewQuestions.q: What is the difference between a dbt test and a Great Expectations expectation, and when would you pick each?
interviewQuestions.a: Both express assertions about data. dbt tests live alongside SQL transformation models and run as queries in the warehouse, so they fit teams already modelling in dbt and testing transformed tables. Great Expectations is a Python library that defines expectation suites against many data sources, including files and dataframes, and produces validation results and documentation. I would choose based on where the team already works and what needs testing: dbt for warehouse models, Great Expectations when validating data outside dbt or at ingestion.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you decide which data checks should block a pipeline and which should only warn?
interviewQuestions.a: By impact and confidence. Checks guarding critical consumers, such as financial reporting or customer-facing figures, and checks with a very low false-positive rate (primary key uniqueness, required fields) should block. Statistical or heuristic checks, such as volume deviating from a trailing average, start as warnings until their thresholds are tuned. Each check needs an owner and a documented response, otherwise warnings get ignored.

roles.codingRequirements: SQL is mandatory and must be strong: joins, aggregates, subqueries, CTEs and window functions. Basic Python or the YAML/Jinja used by tools such as dbt is very helpful. Full software engineering skills are not required for most positions.
commonMistakes: Checking only row counts, which misses wrong values, duplicates that offset drops, and broken joins
Writing checks without agreeing thresholds and owners with the business, so alerts are ignored
Testing only on clean sample data and never on late, duplicated or malformed records
Treating a passing test suite as proof the data is correct rather than evidence that known rules hold
readinessCriteria: Can write a window-function query to find duplicates and gaps without reference material
Has built an automated data test suite that runs in a pipeline or CI job and fails on violations
Can explain each data quality dimension with a concrete check
Has performed a source-to-target reconciliation and explained the discrepancies found

roles.title: ETL Test Engineer
roles.overview: An ETL Test Engineer verifies the extract, transform and load processes that move data between systems. They test mapping rules, transformation logic, incremental loads and error handling, and prove through reconciliation that what arrives in the target matches what left the source after the documented transformations.
responsibilities: Analyse source-to-target mapping documents and derive test cases for every transformation rule
Validate full and incremental loads, including change data capture and slowly changing dimension behaviour
Reconcile source and target on counts, aggregates and row-level samples
Test rejection and error handling for malformed, duplicate or late-arriving records
Verify job scheduling, dependencies, restartability and idempotency of reruns
Prepare test data that exercises boundaries, nulls, encodings and type conversions
Report defects with the failing query, affected records and the mapping rule involved

essential: Advanced SQL including set operations (EXCEPT/MINUS) for comparisons
Reading source-to-target mapping specifications
Understanding of full versus incremental loads and change data capture
Test case design for transformation rules
roleSpecific: Slowly changing dimension types (especially Type 1 and Type 2) and how to test them
Reconciliation techniques across heterogeneous databases
Familiarity with an ETL or orchestration tool such as Apache Airflow, dbt or a commercial ETL suite
optional: Python scripting for file and API source comparisons
Experience with columnar or cloud data warehouses

prerequisites: Understanding of relational databases and keys

beginner.title: Understand ETL flows and mapping
goals: Explain extract, transform and load stages and where defects typically enter
Write test cases directly from a mapping document for direct, derived and lookup columns
Compare source and target with EXCEPT queries in both directions
Validate data type conversions and truncation on boundary values

intermediate.title: Incremental loads and error paths
goals: Test an incremental load by inserting, updating and deleting source rows between runs
Verify SCD Type 2 history rows: effective dates, current flag and no overlapping periods
Test that rerunning a failed job does not duplicate data
Validate that rejected records land in an error table with a reason

advanced.title: Automating ETL verification
goals: Build a reusable reconciliation framework parameterised by source and target tables
Run ETL regression checks in a CI pipeline against a containerised database
Define entry and exit criteria for ETL releases
Estimate ETL test effort from mapping complexity

exercises: Write a mapping-based test case set for a customer table with concatenated names, a lookup-coded country and a derived age band
Simulate two incremental loads and verify inserts, updates and deletes are applied exactly once
Test an SCD Type 2 dimension for overlapping effective date ranges with a self-join
Write a two-way EXCEPT comparison between a staging and target table and interpret the output

sampleProject.title: Incremental load test harness
sampleProject.description: Build a small pipeline (Python or dbt) that loads a customer source table into a dimension with SCD Type 2 history. Write an automated harness that seeds source changes between runs, executes the load, and asserts on counts, history correctness, idempotent reruns and rejected-record handling. Run it in Docker so it is reproducible.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test an incremental load?
interviewQuestions.a: I establish a baseline with an initial full load, then make controlled changes in the source: new rows, updates to tracked and untracked columns, deletes if they are supported, and records with timestamps at the watermark boundary. After the next run I verify only the expected rows changed, nothing was duplicated, the watermark advanced correctly and late-arriving records are handled per the specification. I also rerun the same load to prove it is idempotent.

interviewQuestions.q: What would you check for an SCD Type 2 dimension?
interviewQuestions.a: Each business key has exactly one current row; effective date ranges per key do not overlap and have no unintended gaps; a change to a tracked attribute closes the old row and opens a new one; a change to an untracked attribute does not create history; surrogate keys are unique; and fact tables reference the version that was valid at the transaction date.

interviewQuestions.q: Source has 1,000,000 rows and target has 999,950. What next?
interviewQuestions.a: Fifty rows is not automatically a defect, so I check the mapping for legitimate filters or rejects. Then I query the reject or error table, and run an anti-join on the business key to list the missing rows. Looking at those rows usually reveals the pattern: nulls in a join key, a failed type conversion, a date outside the load window or an inner join to a missing dimension member. The defect report includes the pattern and the rule involved.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you compare data between two different database engines?
interviewQuestions.a: Direct joins are not possible, so I compare at levels: counts and aggregates per partition first, then hashed row fingerprints per key computed consistently on both sides (watching for differences in null handling, trimming, decimal precision and time zones), and finally full row comparisons only for partitions that differ. A script, for example in Python, can pull both sides and diff them for smaller volumes.

interviewQuestions.q: Why does idempotency matter for ETL jobs and how do you test it?
interviewQuestions.a: Jobs fail and get retried, sometimes partway through. If a rerun inserts the same rows again, totals double silently. I test it by running the same load twice with no source changes and asserting the target is unchanged, and by killing a job midway, rerunning it and verifying the final state equals a clean single run.

roles.codingRequirements: Advanced SQL is required. Python or shell scripting is commonly expected for building reusable comparison utilities, but deep application programming is not usually required.
commonMistakes: Comparing only total counts, which can hide equal numbers of dropped and duplicated rows
Testing a single full load and never testing incremental runs, reruns or late data
Ignoring rejected records instead of verifying each reject has a correct reason
Not checking precision, rounding and time-zone conversions in transformation rules
readinessCriteria: Can derive test cases from a mapping document for direct, derived and lookup columns
Has tested an incremental load including updates, deletes and reruns
Can write two-way EXCEPT and anti-join reconciliation queries from memory
Can explain and test SCD Type 1 and Type 2 behaviour

roles.title: Data Warehouse Tester
roles.overview: A Data Warehouse Tester validates the dimensional models, facts, aggregates and semantic layers that analytical reporting is built on. Beyond loading correctness, they check that grain, conformed dimensions and business metric definitions are right, so the same question gets the same answer everywhere.
responsibilities: Verify fact table grain and that measures are additive, semi-additive or non-additive as designed
Test dimension integrity: unknown members, conformed dimensions and history handling
Validate aggregate and summary tables against detailed facts
Check business metric definitions against agreed documentation
Test partitioning, data retention and backfill processes
Run regression comparisons when models are refactored
Monitor data freshness against agreed service levels

essential: Advanced SQL including window functions and CTEs
Dimensional modelling concepts: facts, dimensions, grain, star schemas
Reconciliation of aggregates against detail
Clear defect reporting with reproducible queries
roleSpecific: Testing slowly changing dimensions and late-arriving facts
Understanding of semi-additive measures such as balances
Performance awareness for large analytical queries

prerequisites: Experience testing data loads or databases

beginner.title: Dimensional modelling basics
goals: Identify the grain of a fact table and test it with a uniqueness query
Explain star versus snowflake schemas
Validate that every fact row joins to a dimension row, including an unknown member
Recompute a summary table from detail and compare

intermediate.title: Facts, history and metrics
goals: Test that point-in-time joins use the dimension version valid at the transaction date
Verify semi-additive measures are not summed across time
Document and test metric definitions with the business owner
Test late-arriving facts and backfills

advanced.title: Warehouse regression and performance
goals: Build before/after comparisons for a model refactor across all key metrics
Identify slow queries and discuss partitioning or clustering impacts with engineers
Define freshness and completeness service levels per subject area
Lead a data release sign-off

tools: A cloud or on-premise data warehouse
exercises: Write a query that proves or disproves the stated grain of a sales fact table
Find fact rows referencing dimension keys that do not exist
Show why summing an account balance across months gives a wrong answer and write the correct query
Compare a monthly summary table against detail facts for twelve months

sampleProject.title: Star schema verification suite
sampleProject.description: Model a small retail star schema (sales fact, date, product, store and customer dimensions with Type 2 history on customer). Write a verification suite that tests grain, referential integrity, point-in-time correctness, aggregate consistency and freshness, and produces a summary of pass/fail per check.

interviewQuestions.q: What is the grain of a fact table and why test it?
interviewQuestions.a: The grain is what one row represents, for example one order line per day. If the grain is violated, for example two rows for the same order line, every sum is inflated. I test it by grouping on the columns that define the grain and asserting no group has more than one row.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you test a refactor of a core data model that should not change any results?
interviewQuestions.a: Run the old and new models side by side on the same data, then compare key metrics by every important dimension and time period, followed by row-level comparison on the keys. Any difference must be explained, either as an intended fix or a defect. I agree tolerances for floating-point differences up front and keep the comparison queries as a regression asset.

interviewQuestions.q: What is a semi-additive measure and what defect does it cause?
interviewQuestions.a: A measure that can be summed across some dimensions but not others, typically balances or inventory levels, which can be summed across accounts but not across time. Summing month-end balances over a year gives a meaningless number; the correct aggregation is usually the last value or an average. I test report queries to make sure they use the right aggregation.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you handle facts that arrive before their dimension member?
interviewQuestions.a: The design usually maps them to an unknown or inferred member so they are not lost, then updates the reference when the dimension row arrives. I test that such facts are loaded rather than dropped, that they point to the inferred member, and that they are correctly re-pointed after the dimension load.

roles.codingRequirements: Advanced SQL is essential. Scripting is helpful but not mandatory. Understanding of data modelling matters more than general programming.
commonMistakes: Never confirming the grain, so duplicated rows inflate every metric
Assuming metric names mean the same thing to every team without written definitions
Testing only the current state of dimensions and ignoring history
Comparing reports to the warehouse with different filters or time zones
readinessCriteria: Can test grain, referential integrity and history on a star schema
Can explain additive, semi-additive and non-additive measures with examples
Has built a before/after regression comparison for a model change
Can reconcile an aggregate table against detail facts

roles.title: Analytics QA Engineer
roles.overview: An Analytics QA Engineer checks that numbers people use to make decisions are trustworthy, from event tracking in the product to dashboards and experiment results. They test instrumentation, metric logic and report behaviour so that a chart reflects what actually happened.
responsibilities: Verify product analytics events fire once, with the correct name, properties and user identifiers
Validate dashboard figures against independent queries on the underlying data
Test metric definitions, filters, time-zone handling and date boundaries in reports
Check experiment (A/B test) assignment, exposure logging and sample ratio
Maintain a tracking plan and flag undocumented or missing events
Test report permissions and row-level security for sensitive data

essential: SQL for independent recomputation of metrics
Understanding of event-based analytics and tracking plans
Basic statistics: rates, distributions and sample sizes
Browser developer tools for inspecting network calls
roleSpecific: A/B test validity checks such as sample ratio mismatch
BI tool behaviour: filters, caching and aggregation settings
Time-zone and date-boundary reasoning
optional: Experience with privacy and consent requirements for tracking

prerequisites: Basic familiarity with web or mobile applications

beginner.title: Events and metrics basics
goals: Inspect analytics network calls in browser developer tools and compare to a tracking plan
Recompute a dashboard metric with SQL and reconcile differences
Test daily metrics around midnight in different time zones
Write a defect report for a missing or duplicated event

intermediate.title: Dashboard and experiment testing
goals: Build a checklist for dashboard filters, drill-downs and empty states
Detect sample ratio mismatch in an experiment dataset
Verify unique-user counts are not double counted across devices or sessions
Test row-level security on a report with two user roles

advanced.title: Analytics quality ownership
goals: Automate tracking-plan validation in end-to-end tests
Define metric certification criteria with analytics owners
Run root cause analysis on a metric discrepancy across systems
Report analytics quality status to product leadership

exercises: Compare five events fired during a sign-up flow against a tracking plan and list discrepancies
Recompute daily active users with SQL and explain any difference from the dashboard
Given experiment assignment counts, decide whether there is a sample ratio mismatch and why it matters
Test a weekly report for correct week-start convention and time zone

sampleProject.title: Tracking plan validator
sampleProject.description: Write a tracking plan for a demo web app (event names, required properties, types). Use Playwright to intercept analytics requests during key flows and assert each expected event fires once with valid properties. Add SQL checks that recompute two dashboard metrics from the stored events and compare them with the reported values.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test that an analytics event is implemented correctly?
interviewQuestions.a: I check it against the tracking plan: correct name, fires on the right trigger exactly once, required properties present with valid types and values, correct user and session identifiers, and respects consent settings. I verify it in the network calls and then in the stored data, because events can be dropped or transformed between client and warehouse.

interviewQuestions.q: What is a sample ratio mismatch and why should a tester care?
interviewQuestions.a: It is when the observed split of users between experiment variants differs from the designed split by more than chance would explain, typically tested with a chi-squared test. It usually indicates a bug in assignment, redirection or exposure logging, which makes the experiment's results unreliable regardless of the measured effect.

interviewQuestions.q: A dashboard and a SQL query disagree on daily active users. What do you check?
interviewQuestions.a: The definition of active, the time zone used for the day boundary, deduplication across devices and anonymous-to-logged-in identity merges, filters such as internal or test users, data freshness and any caching in the BI tool. I align them one at a time until the numbers match and document which definition is authoritative.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test row-level security in a reporting tool?
interviewQuestions.a: I create test users in each role, check that each sees only permitted rows and that totals reflect only those rows, try access via export, drill-through and direct URLs, and confirm that changing role membership takes effect. Aggregates are a common leak, so I verify totals as well as row lists.

roles.codingRequirements: SQL is required. Light JavaScript or TypeScript is helpful for automated event checks. Statistical programming is optional.
commonMistakes: Verifying an event fires in the browser but never checking it arrives correctly in the warehouse
Ignoring time zones and week-start conventions in date-based metrics
Including internal or test traffic in production metrics
Trusting a dashboard total without an independent recomputation
readinessCriteria: Can validate events against a tracking plan using browser tools
Can independently recompute a dashboard metric and explain differences
Can explain sample ratio mismatch and how to check for it
Has tested row-level security for at least two roles

roles.title: AI Quality Engineer
roles.overview: An AI Quality Engineer designs how AI-powered features are evaluated and tested across their lifecycle. Because model outputs are probabilistic, the role combines classic software testing of the surrounding system with evaluation datasets, quality metrics, human review and production monitoring, and is honest about what each method can and cannot show.
responsibilities: Define quality criteria for AI features with product owners, including failure modes that are unacceptable
Build and maintain evaluation datasets with labelled expected behaviour and edge cases
Design automated evaluation pipelines that run on model, prompt or data changes
Test the deterministic parts of AI systems: input validation, fallbacks, timeouts, rate limits and logging
Coordinate human review and calibrate automated graders against human judgments
Assess safety, fairness and privacy risks and test for them
Monitor production quality signals and feed failures back into evaluation sets

essential: Software testing fundamentals and test design
Evaluation design: datasets, metrics, baselines and regression thresholds
Python for scripting evaluations and analysing results
Understanding of how ML and LLM systems fail: non-determinism, overfitting, distribution shift
roleSpecific: Classification metrics such as precision, recall and confusion matrices
LLM evaluation methods including rubric grading and their limitations
Safety testing for prompt injection and harmful outputs
optional: Familiarity with AI risk management frameworks

prerequisites: Experience as a tester or developer

beginner.title: Testing AI-powered features
goals: Explain why exact-match assertions rarely work for model outputs and what to use instead
Test the non-model parts of an AI feature: validation, error handling, timeouts and fallbacks
Create a small labelled evaluation set covering typical, edge and adversarial inputs
Compute precision and recall for a simple classifier

intermediate.title: Evaluation pipelines
goals: Build an evaluation script that scores a model or prompt version against a fixed dataset
Set regression thresholds and run evaluations in CI on prompt or model changes
Calibrate an automated grader against a sample of human labels
Test for prompt injection and data leakage

advanced.title: AI quality strategy
goals: Write an AI test strategy covering offline evaluation, human review and production monitoring
Define risk tiers for AI features and matching evaluation depth
Design a feedback loop from production failures into evaluation sets
Report AI quality with confidence intervals rather than single numbers

exercises: Write a 30-item evaluation set for a support-ticket classifier and compute per-class precision and recall
List ten failure modes for a summarisation feature and say how each would be detected
Compare two prompt versions on the same dataset and decide whether the difference is meaningful
Write test cases for the fallback behaviour when the model API times out

sampleProject.title: Evaluation harness for an AI ticket triage feature
sampleProject.description: Build a Python harness that runs a labelled set of support tickets through a classifier or LLM prompt, computes per-category precision, recall and a confusion matrix, flags regressions against a stored baseline, and runs in CI. Include adversarial inputs and a written note on the limits of the evaluation.

interviewQuestions.q: How is testing an AI feature different from testing a conventional feature?
interviewQuestions.a: Outputs are probabilistic and often have many acceptable answers, so I test statistically against an evaluation set with metrics and thresholds rather than single exact assertions. The surrounding system is still conventional and gets conventional tests. Quality can also change without code changes, through model updates or shifting input data, so production monitoring is part of testing rather than an afterthought.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you build a good evaluation dataset?
interviewQuestions.a: Start from real or realistic inputs representing the actual usage distribution, add edge cases and known failure modes, label expected outcomes with clear guidelines, measure agreement between labellers, keep it versioned and separate from any data used for tuning prompts or training, and grow it with production failures. Its size should be enough that differences you care about are distinguishable from noise.

interviewQuestions.q: What are the limitations of using an LLM as a judge?
interviewQuestions.a: LLM graders can prefer longer answers, favour particular positions or styles, be inconsistent between runs, miss factual errors they cannot verify, and share blind spots with the model being evaluated. I mitigate this with specific rubrics, checking agreement against human labels on a sample, randomising order in pairwise comparisons, and keeping deterministic checks wherever possible. I treat the judge as an instrument that needs calibration.

interviewQuestions.q: A new model version scores 2 points higher on your evaluation. Do you ship it?
interviewQuestions.a: Not on that number alone. I check whether the difference is larger than run-to-run variation, look at per-category results for regressions hidden by the average, review safety and latency or cost changes, and inspect a sample of changed outputs. If critical categories regressed, the aggregate improvement does not justify shipping.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you test for bias in a model that scores loan applications?
interviewQuestions.a: Working with legal and domain experts, I identify relevant groups and fairness metrics, for example comparing false positive and false negative rates or approval rates across groups. I evaluate on data with sufficient representation of each group, check proxies for protected attributes, and report that different fairness metrics can conflict so the choice is a documented decision, not a purely technical one.

roles.codingRequirements: Python is required for evaluation scripts and data analysis. You do not need to train models from scratch, but you must be comfortable reading model APIs, manipulating datasets and writing automated tests.
commonMistakes: Reporting a single average score without per-category breakdowns or variance
Tuning prompts against the same evaluation set used to report quality, which inflates results
Trusting an LLM judge without checking it against human labels
Ignoring the deterministic system around the model, such as timeouts and fallbacks
readinessCriteria: Has built a versioned evaluation dataset and an automated scoring script
Can explain precision, recall and the trade-off between them with an example
Can describe at least three limitations of LLM-as-judge and mitigations
Has written test cases for prompt injection and fallback behaviour

roles.title: LLM Application Tester
roles.overview: An LLM Application Tester tests products built on large language models, such as assistants, summarisers and content generators. They design test sets and rubrics, probe for hallucinations, prompt injection and unsafe outputs, and check that the application handles the model's variability, latency and failures gracefully.
responsibilities: Design scenario-based test sets with expected behaviours and grading rubrics
Test factual accuracy and identify hallucinated content against source material
Probe direct and indirect prompt injection, system prompt leakage and jailbreak attempts in authorised test environments
Verify output format constraints such as valid JSON or required fields
Test conversation handling: context limits, multi-turn consistency and refusals
Check latency, streaming, timeouts, retries and cost-related limits
Run regression evaluations when prompts, models or parameters change

essential: Test design for open-ended outputs: rubrics, properties and acceptable variation
Understanding of LLM behaviour: tokens, context windows, temperature, non-determinism
Exploratory testing skills
Clear documentation of failures with prompts, settings and outputs
roleSpecific: Prompt injection and jailbreak test techniques
Hallucination detection against reference sources
Structured output validation, for example with JSON Schema
optional: Accessibility and localisation testing of AI responses

beginner.title: Exploring LLM behaviour
goals: Document how output changes with temperature and repeated runs for the same prompt
Write exploratory charters for hallucination, refusal and format-following
Create a rubric with three to five scored criteria for one feature
Report an LLM defect with full reproduction context

intermediate.title: Systematic LLM evaluation
goals: Build a test set of at least 50 scenarios with expected behaviours
Validate structured outputs automatically with a JSON Schema
Run a prompt injection test suite including indirect injection through retrieved or uploaded content
Compare two prompt versions with the same test set

advanced.title: Automated and production evaluation
goals: Automate evaluations in CI with thresholds per category
Calibrate an LLM judge against human ratings and document agreement
Define monitoring signals for production, such as user feedback and refusal rates
Test retrieval-augmented features for grounding

exercises: Write 15 prompt injection test cases, including instructions hidden in a document the assistant summarises
Run the same prompt ten times and categorise the variation in outputs
Create a rubric for a meeting summariser and score ten outputs with a peer, then compare agreement
Validate that an extraction feature returns schema-valid JSON for 30 varied inputs

sampleProject.title: LLM assistant evaluation pack
sampleProject.description: For a small LLM-backed Q&A or summarisation app you build or are authorised to test, create a versioned test set covering normal use, edge cases, hallucination traps, format constraints and prompt injection. Write a Python runner that executes it, applies schema checks and rubric grading, and produces a report comparing two prompt versions per category.

interviewQuestions.q: What is prompt injection, and how would you test for it?
interviewQuestions.a: It is when untrusted input contains instructions that override or subvert the application's intended instructions. Direct injection comes from the user; indirect injection arrives through content the model processes, such as web pages, documents or tool results. I test both, with attempts to reveal the system prompt, ignore rules, exfiltrate data or trigger actions, and verify mitigations such as input separation, output filtering and least-privilege tool access. Because no mitigation is complete, I also check the impact is contained when one succeeds.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test for hallucinations?
interviewQuestions.a: I create inputs where the correct answer is known or bounded by a source, including questions whose answer is not in the source. I check that claims are supported by the source, that the model says it does not know when appropriate, and that citations actually support the statements. Automated checks can flag unsupported claims, but I verify a sample by hand because automated grounding checks are imperfect.

interviewQuestions.q: Outputs differ every run. How can a test be repeatable?
interviewQuestions.a: I make the test assert properties, not exact text: required facts present, format valid, no forbidden content, rubric score above threshold. I fix settings where possible, run multiple samples for important cases and report pass rates. Repeatability comes from the fixed test set, rubric and thresholds rather than identical outputs.

interviewQuestions.q: What non-model aspects of an LLM application do you test?
interviewQuestions.a: Input length limits and truncation, timeouts and retries, behaviour when the provider returns errors or rate-limits, streaming and cancellation, logging that does not store sensitive data inappropriately, authentication and authorisation around conversations, cost controls, and the user experience when the model refuses or fails.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you report LLM quality to a product manager?
interviewQuestions.a: By category of scenario, with pass rates against agreed rubrics, notable failure examples, safety results and the trend versus the previous version. I state the size and composition of the test set and the known limits of the evaluation so a single number is not over-interpreted.

roles.codingRequirements: Coding is not strictly required for exploratory LLM testing, but Python for calling APIs and running evaluations is strongly preferred for most roles. JSON and basic API skills are expected.
commonMistakes: Running a prompt once and drawing conclusions from a single output
Testing only direct prompt injection and forgetting injection through documents or tool results
Accepting fluent, confident answers without checking them against a source
Changing the test set between versions, making comparisons meaningless
readinessCriteria: Has built and versioned a scenario test set with rubrics for an LLM feature
Can demonstrate direct and indirect prompt injection test cases in an authorised environment
Can explain why property-based assertions are used for non-deterministic outputs
Has automated schema validation for structured model outputs

roles.title: ML Model Testing Specialist
roles.overview: An ML Model Testing Specialist evaluates predictive machine learning models such as classifiers, rankers and forecasters. They check data splits, metric choice, robustness, fairness across groups and drift after deployment, and make sure model quality claims are supported by sound evaluation.
responsibilities: Review training, validation and test splits for leakage and representativeness
Choose and compute evaluation metrics appropriate to the task and business cost of errors
Perform slice-based evaluation to find subgroups where the model underperforms
Assess fairness metrics across relevant groups with domain and legal input
Test robustness to noisy, missing or out-of-range features
Validate that model serving produces the same predictions as offline evaluation
Define data and prediction drift monitoring and retraining triggers

essential: Python with pandas and scikit-learn
ML evaluation metrics: precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC, calibration, regression errors
Statistics: sampling, confidence intervals, distribution comparison
Understanding of overfitting and data leakage
roleSpecific: Slice-based and fairness evaluation
Data and concept drift detection
Training-serving skew testing
optional: Experiment tracking and model registry tools

beginner.title: Evaluation fundamentals
goals: Compute a confusion matrix and derive precision, recall and F1 by hand and in code
Explain why accuracy misleads on imbalanced data
Identify target leakage in a feature list
Write unit tests for feature transformation functions

intermediate.title: Slices, fairness and robustness
goals: Evaluate a model per segment and flag segments below threshold
Compute and compare error rates across groups and explain metric trade-offs
Test model behaviour on missing values, extreme values and unseen categories
Test that offline and served predictions match for the same inputs

advanced.title: Production model quality
goals: Design drift monitoring for input features and prediction distributions
Define model release criteria including fairness and robustness gates
Run statistically sound comparisons between model versions
Automate model evaluation in a CI pipeline

exercises: Train a simple classifier on an imbalanced public dataset and show why accuracy is misleading
Evaluate the model on three slices and identify the weakest one
Simulate a shift in one feature's distribution and detect it with a statistical test
Write pytest tests for a feature engineering pipeline including null and unseen-category inputs

sampleProject.title: Model validation report for a churn classifier
sampleProject.description: Using a public tabular dataset, train a baseline classifier and produce a validation report: leakage review, metric choice justified by error costs, slice evaluation, a fairness comparison on an available attribute with limitations stated, robustness tests and a drift detection demo. Include automated pytest checks that fail if key metrics fall below thresholds.

interviewQuestions.q: What is data leakage and how do you detect it?
interviewQuestions.a: Leakage is when information that would not be available at prediction time influences training, giving optimistic evaluation results. Examples are features derived from the target, future data in time-series splits, or the same entity in train and test. I detect it by reviewing how each feature is produced and when it is available, using time-based splits where appropriate, checking for suspiciously predictive features and grouping by entity when splitting.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you choose an evaluation metric?
interviewQuestions.a: From the cost of different errors. If missing a positive is costly, recall matters; if false alarms are costly, precision matters; if a threshold will be tuned later, a threshold-independent metric like ROC or precision-recall AUC helps for comparison; if probabilities drive decisions, calibration matters. I always report more than one metric and agree the primary metric with stakeholders before evaluating.

interviewQuestions.q: What is the difference between data drift and concept drift?
interviewQuestions.a: Data drift is a change in the input distribution, for example a new customer segment. Concept drift is a change in the relationship between inputs and the target, for example customer behaviour changing so the same features predict differently. Data drift can be detected from inputs alone; concept drift usually needs fresh labels or proxy outcomes to detect.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you test a model for fairness?
interviewQuestions.a: With domain and legal stakeholders I identify groups and the harm of interest, choose metrics such as differences in selection rate or in false positive and false negative rates, evaluate with enough samples per group to be meaningful, and check proxies for sensitive attributes. I report that some fairness criteria cannot be satisfied simultaneously, so the chosen criterion and its trade-offs must be documented decisions.

interviewQuestions.q: What is training-serving skew and how do you test for it?
interviewQuestions.a: It is when features are computed differently in production than in training, so the served model sees different inputs than it was evaluated on. I test by sending the same raw records through the offline feature pipeline and the serving path and comparing features and predictions, and by monitoring feature distributions in production against training.

roles.codingRequirements: Python is required, including pandas and a common ML library. You need to be able to train simple models, compute metrics and write automated tests. Deep learning expertise is role-dependent.
commonMistakes: Using accuracy on imbalanced data
Random splits on time-dependent data, leaking future information into training
Reporting only aggregate metrics and missing poorly served subgroups
Treating a fairness metric as a purely technical choice without stakeholder input
readinessCriteria: Can identify leakage in a feature set and propose a correct split
Has produced slice-based evaluation and a fairness comparison with stated limitations
Can explain data drift versus concept drift and how each is detected
Has automated model metric thresholds in tests

roles.title: RAG Application Evaluator
roles.overview: A RAG Application Evaluator measures and improves retrieval-augmented generation systems, where a model answers using documents retrieved from a knowledge base. They evaluate retrieval and generation separately, so a team knows whether a bad answer came from finding the wrong content or from misusing the right content.
responsibilities: Build question sets with known relevant documents and reference answers
Measure retrieval quality with metrics such as recall at k, precision at k and mean reciprocal rank
Evaluate answer faithfulness to retrieved context and answer relevance to the question
Test chunking, embedding and filtering choices for their effect on retrieval
Verify access control so users only retrieve documents they are permitted to see
Test handling of questions with no answer in the corpus and of conflicting or outdated documents
Track evaluation results across index, model and prompt changes

essential: Understanding of the RAG pipeline: ingestion, chunking, embedding, retrieval, re-ranking and generation
Information retrieval metrics
Evaluation dataset design
Python for running evaluations
roleSpecific: Faithfulness and groundedness evaluation, automated and human
Testing document-level permissions in retrieval
Indirect prompt injection through indexed content

beginner.title: RAG anatomy and failure points
goals: Diagram a RAG pipeline and list failure modes at each stage
Write 20 questions with their known relevant documents
Manually judge whether answers are supported by retrieved chunks
Test questions whose answer is absent from the corpus

intermediate.title: Measuring retrieval and generation
goals: Compute recall at k and mean reciprocal rank for a question set
Compare two chunking strategies on the same question set
Score faithfulness with an automated grader and check it against manual judgments
Test that permission filters prevent retrieval of restricted documents

advanced.title: Continuous RAG evaluation
goals: Automate retrieval and answer evaluations in CI on index or prompt changes
Test indirect prompt injection planted in indexed documents
Define production signals such as unanswered rate and citation click-through for review
Write an evaluation strategy that separates retrieval and generation ownership

tools: A vector database or search engine
exercises: Compute recall at 5 and MRR by hand for five questions with given retrieved lists
Create ten questions with no answer in the corpus and check whether the system declines
Plant an instruction in a test document and check if the assistant follows it when the document is retrieved
Compare answers before and after changing chunk size, categorising each change

sampleProject.title: RAG evaluation harness
sampleProject.description: Index a corpus of public documentation you are allowed to use, build a simple RAG pipeline, and create a labelled set of questions with relevant document ids and reference answers. Write a harness that reports retrieval metrics, faithfulness and answer relevance separately, includes unanswerable and adversarial questions, and compares two chunking configurations.

interviewQuestions.q: Why evaluate retrieval and generation separately?
interviewQuestions.a: Because the fixes are different. If the relevant passage was never retrieved, changing the prompt cannot help; you need better chunking, embeddings, query rewriting or re-ranking. If the right passage was retrieved but the answer is wrong or unsupported, the generation step is at fault. Separate metrics tell the team where to spend effort.

interviewQuestions.q: Explain recall at k and mean reciprocal rank.
interviewQuestions.a: Recall at k is the share of relevant documents that appear in the top k results, averaged across questions. Mean reciprocal rank averages, over questions, one divided by the rank of the first relevant result, so it rewards putting a relevant result near the top. Recall at k matters when the generator reads all k chunks; MRR matters when the first result dominates.

interviewQuestions.q: What is faithfulness and how do you measure it?
interviewQuestions.a: Faithfulness is whether every claim in the answer is supported by the retrieved context. It is usually measured by splitting the answer into claims and checking each against the context, either by human reviewers or by an LLM grader. Automated graders should be validated against human judgments on a sample, since they can miss subtle unsupported claims.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you test access control in a RAG system?
interviewQuestions.a: Create documents with different permissions and test users in each group, then ask questions whose answers exist only in restricted documents. Verify the restricted content is neither retrieved nor paraphrased in the answer or citations, and that permission changes take effect in the index. Filtering must happen at retrieval time, not only in the user interface.

interviewQuestions.q: How should a RAG system handle a question the corpus cannot answer?
interviewQuestions.a: It should say it cannot find the answer, or ask a clarifying question, instead of answering from the model's general knowledge if the product requires grounded answers. I include unanswerable questions in the evaluation set and track the rate at which the system correctly declines versus fabricates.

roles.codingRequirements: Python is required to build datasets, run pipelines and compute metrics. Understanding of APIs and JSON is expected. You do not need to build embedding models.
commonMistakes: Judging only the final answer and never inspecting what was retrieved
Leaving out unanswerable questions, so fabrication is never measured
Building questions by copying sentences from documents, which overstates retrieval quality
Ignoring document permissions during retrieval testing
readinessCriteria: Can compute retrieval metrics for a labelled question set
Has measured faithfulness and validated an automated grader against human judgments
Has tested retrieval permissions and indirect prompt injection
Can explain how to localise a bad answer to retrieval or generation

roles.title: AI Agent Testing Engineer
roles.overview: An AI Agent Testing Engineer tests systems where a model plans and takes actions through tools, such as calling APIs, editing files or browsing. Because agents act in the world, the role focuses on tool-call correctness, task completion across multi-step trajectories, permission boundaries and safe failure behaviour in sandboxed environments.
responsibilities: Design task suites with defined goals, environments and success checks
Evaluate tool selection and argument correctness at each step of an agent trajectory
Test safety controls: least-privilege permissions, confirmation for risky actions and spending or rate limits
Probe indirect prompt injection through tool outputs, web pages and files
Test error handling when tools fail, time out or return unexpected data
Build sandboxed and mocked environments so tests do not affect real systems
Analyse trajectory logs to classify failures and feed them into regression suites

essential: Python or TypeScript for test harnesses
API testing and mocking skills
LLM evaluation fundamentals
Security mindset: least privilege, untrusted input, auditability
roleSpecific: Trajectory and task-completion evaluation
Tool and function-calling schema validation
Sandboxing and environment reset for repeatable agent tests

prerequisites: Experience testing LLM applications or APIs

beginner.title: How agents work and fail
goals: Describe the plan, act and observe loop and where errors enter
Validate tool-call arguments against their JSON schemas
Write five tasks with clear, checkable end states
Test agent behaviour when a tool returns an error

intermediate.title: Task suites and safety tests
goals: Build a sandboxed environment that resets between runs
Measure task success rate over repeated runs per task
Test that destructive actions require confirmation and stay within permitted scope
Run indirect prompt injection tests through tool outputs

advanced.title: Agent evaluation at scale
goals: Automate agent evaluations in CI with per-task pass rates and cost and step budgets
Classify trajectory failures into planning, tool-use and recovery categories
Design guardrail and monitoring requirements for production agents
Write a risk-based test strategy for an agent with access to real systems

exercises: Write a mock tool server that injects errors and latency, and observe how the agent recovers
Define success checks for a 'book a meeting' task using the final calendar state rather than the agent's message
Craft a tool output containing hidden instructions and test whether the agent follows them
Run one task 20 times and report success rate, step count distribution and failure categories

sampleProject.title: Sandboxed agent evaluation suite
sampleProject.description: Build a small agent with three tools (file read, file write in a sandbox folder, mock HTTP API). Create a task suite with state-based success checks, error-injecting mocks, permission-boundary tests and indirect prompt injection cases. The runner repeats each task several times in a resettable container and reports success rates, budgets used and categorised failures.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you decide whether an agent completed a task?
interviewQuestions.a: By checking the resulting environment state against the goal, for example the record exists with the right values, not by trusting the agent's final message. I also check for side effects outside the goal, budgets used and whether any forbidden action occurred. Because outcomes vary, I run tasks multiple times and report success rates.

interviewQuestions.q: What safety tests would you run on an agent that can send emails?
interviewQuestions.a: In a sandbox with a mock mail service: does it require confirmation before sending, does it refuse to send to recipients outside an allowed scope, can instructions inside an incoming email trick it into forwarding data, are rate limits enforced, is every action logged for audit, and does it stop cleanly when a step fails. Real external sends are never part of the test.

interviewQuestions.q: Why is indirect prompt injection especially dangerous for agents?
interviewQuestions.a: Agents read untrusted content from tools and then take actions, so injected instructions can turn into real effects such as data exfiltration or unauthorised changes. Mitigations include least-privilege tools, separating data from instructions, human confirmation for high-impact actions and output checks, and testing must assume some injection will succeed and verify that impact is contained.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you make agent tests repeatable?
interviewQuestions.a: Reset the environment to a known state before each run, mock or stub external services, fix model settings where possible, record full trajectories, and measure pass rates over repeated runs rather than single outcomes. Flaky tasks are analysed to see whether the variability is in the agent or in the environment.

interviewQuestions.q: What do you look for in a failed trajectory?
interviewQuestions.a: Where it went wrong: misunderstanding the goal, choosing the wrong tool, wrong arguments, misreading a tool result, failing to recover from an error, looping, or stopping early. Categorising failures this way tells the team whether to fix prompts, tool descriptions, tool error messages or guardrails.

roles.codingRequirements: Programming is required: Python or TypeScript to build harnesses, mock tools and environments, and analyse logs. Comfort with APIs, JSON schemas and containers is expected.
commonMistakes: Running agent tests against real systems instead of sandboxes
Accepting the agent's own claim of success without checking state
Testing only happy paths and never failing tools
Judging from single runs instead of success rates
readinessCriteria: Has built a resettable sandbox and a task suite with state-based success checks
Can design permission-boundary and indirect prompt injection tests
Can report agent results as success rates with categorised failures
Can explain least-privilege design for agent tools

roles.title: DevOps and CI/CD Test Engineer
roles.overview: A DevOps and CI/CD Test Engineer makes automated testing a reliable, fast part of the delivery pipeline. They design which tests run at which pipeline stage, keep test environments reproducible with containers, tackle flaky tests, and give the team trustworthy signals about whether a change is safe to release.
responsibilities: Design pipeline test stages: fast checks on every commit, broader suites on merge and pre-release
Build and maintain CI jobs that run unit, API, UI and non-functional tests
Containerise test dependencies so environments are reproducible locally and in CI
Parallelise and shard test suites to keep feedback times acceptable
Track and reduce flaky tests with quarantine and fix processes
Publish test reports, artifacts and trends that developers actually use
Collaborate on deployment strategies such as staged rollouts and post-deploy smoke tests

essential: A CI system such as GitHub Actions or Jenkins
Docker basics: images, containers, volumes and networks
Test automation in at least one language
Git workflows including branches and pull requests
roleSpecific: Pipeline design and test selection by stage
Flaky test diagnosis
Infrastructure as code awareness, for example reading Terraform plans

beginner.title: CI basics
goals: Create a pipeline that installs dependencies and runs tests on every pull request
Publish test reports and failure artifacts from CI
Run a dependency such as a database in a container for tests
Explain the test pyramid in terms of pipeline stages

intermediate.title: Fast and reliable pipelines
goals: Shard a test suite across parallel jobs and measure the time saved
Set up a flaky-test quarantine with an owner and a deadline
Add post-deployment smoke tests
Cache dependencies safely

advanced.title: Delivery quality strategy
goals: Design quality gates per stage with clear pass and fail rules
Integrate performance and security checks without blocking every commit
Track pipeline metrics such as duration, failure causes and flake rate
Plan testing for staged rollouts and rollback

exercises: Write a GitHub Actions workflow that runs API tests against a service and database started with Docker Compose
Take a 20-minute test suite and design a sharding plan to bring feedback under 10 minutes
Diagnose three flaky tests from CI logs and classify their causes
Add a post-deploy smoke test job that runs only on the main branch

sampleProject.title: Containerised test pipeline
sampleProject.description: For a small web app with an API and database, build a CI pipeline with stages for lint and unit tests, API tests against containerised services, sharded UI tests and a smoke test after a mock deployment. Publish reports and artifacts, add a flaky-test quarantine label, and document pipeline duration before and after optimisation.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you decide which tests run on every commit and which run later?
interviewQuestions.a: Based on feedback speed and the risk each test covers. Fast, reliable unit and component tests and critical API checks run on every commit; broader integration and UI suites run on merge or in parallel; long-running performance, full regression and cross-browser suites run nightly or before release. The goal is quick, trustworthy feedback early while still covering high-risk areas before release.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you deal with flaky tests in CI?
interviewQuestions.a: Measure them first by tracking failures that pass on retry. Quarantine known flaky tests so they do not block merges, but give each an owner and deadline so quarantine does not become a graveyard. Then diagnose causes: timing and waits, shared test data, order dependence, environment instability. Automatic retries hide the problem, so if used they must be reported.

interviewQuestions.q: Why use containers for test environments?
interviewQuestions.a: They make dependencies reproducible: the same database version and configuration locally and in CI, started fresh for each run, which removes 'works on my machine' differences and leftover state. They also make parallel isolated environments cheap.

interviewQuestions.q: What does infrastructure as code mean for a test engineer?
interviewQuestions.a: Environments are defined in versioned files, such as Terraform or Kubernetes manifests, so they can be reviewed, recreated and tested. A test engineer should be able to read a plan to understand what will change, request test environments that match production configuration, and include configuration changes in risk assessment.

interviewQuestions.q: A pipeline that took 10 minutes now takes 35. How do you approach it?
interviewQuestions.a: Look at job timing history to find which stage grew, then check for causes like lost caches, new slow tests, serialised jobs, slower runners or retries. Fix the biggest contributor first, then add a duration budget and alerting so the regression does not return unnoticed.

roles.codingRequirements: Scripting and test automation coding are required: YAML pipeline definitions, shell and at least one programming language for tests. Infrastructure as code is usually read rather than written in this role.
commonMistakes: Adding automatic retries to hide flaky tests instead of fixing them
Running every test on every commit until feedback is too slow to be useful
Sharing a single mutable test environment across parallel jobs
Failing to keep logs, screenshots and traces as artifacts for failed runs
readinessCriteria: Has built a working CI pipeline with containerised dependencies and published reports
Can explain a staged testing strategy mapped to pipeline stages
Has diagnosed and fixed at least one flaky test with a documented cause
Can read a CI configuration and explain its triggers, jobs and caching

roles.title: Cloud QA Engineer
roles.overview: A Cloud QA Engineer tests applications that run on cloud infrastructure and managed services. Beyond functional behaviour, they verify configuration, scaling, resilience to service failures, identity and permissions, and cost-aware environment usage, working closely with platform and operations teams.
responsibilities: Test applications across environments and validate configuration differences
Verify identity and access permissions follow least privilege for services and users
Test autoscaling, health checks and recovery from instance or zone failures
Validate integrations with managed services such as queues, storage and databases
Use observability data (logs, metrics, traces) to verify behaviour and investigate failures
Create and tear down ephemeral test environments to control cost
Test backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures

essential: Core cloud concepts: regions, zones, compute, storage, networking and identity
API and integration testing
Containers and basic orchestration concepts
Reading logs, metrics and traces
roleSpecific: Testing distributed systems failure modes: timeouts, retries, partial failures
Infrastructure as code awareness
Backup and recovery testing

prerequisites: Experience testing web applications or APIs

beginner.title: Cloud fundamentals for testers
goals: Explain regions, availability zones, managed services and shared responsibility
Deploy a containerised app to a test environment and run API tests against it
Find a request in logs using a correlation id
Verify a service account cannot access resources outside its role

intermediate.title: Distributed behaviour and resilience
goals: Test retry and timeout behaviour when a managed dependency is slow or unavailable
Verify autoscaling triggers under a controlled load test
Test message queue handling for duplicates and poison messages
Create ephemeral environments from infrastructure definitions

advanced.title: Cloud quality strategy
goals: Run a disaster recovery test and compare results against recovery objectives
Define environment parity rules between staging and production
Use observability data for test oracles and release decisions
Plan controlled failure experiments with the reliability team

tools: A major cloud provider console and CLI
exercises: Compare two environment configurations and list differences that could affect test results
Simulate a slow downstream dependency and verify timeout and retry behaviour
Write tests for a queue consumer covering duplicate and malformed messages
Perform a restore from backup in a test environment and record time and data loss

sampleProject.title: Resilience tests for a containerised service
sampleProject.description: Deploy a small API with a database and a message queue to a local Kubernetes cluster or a cloud free tier you control. Write API and integration tests, verify health checks restart a failed container, test behaviour when the queue or database is unavailable, run a small load test to observe scaling, and tear the environment down with scripts.

interviewQuestions.q: What is different about testing in the cloud compared with a single server?
interviewQuestions.a: The system is distributed and dynamic: instances come and go, network calls fail partially, managed services have their own limits and behaviours, and configuration and identity are part of the system. Testing therefore covers retries, timeouts, scaling, permissions and configuration drift, not only functional behaviour, and relies more on observability.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test least-privilege permissions?
interviewQuestions.a: For each service identity, list the actions it should perform, then test both that those succeed and that adjacent actions it should not perform are denied, such as reading another bucket or deleting resources. I also check policies for wildcards and confirm that secrets are not exposed through logs or environment dumps.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you test a backup and restore process?
interviewQuestions.a: Restore into an isolated environment, verify data integrity with counts and checksums against known reference data, measure how long it took and how much data was lost versus the recovery time and point objectives, and confirm the application works on the restored data. A backup that has never been restored is unproven.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you keep cloud test environments affordable?
interviewQuestions.a: Create them on demand from infrastructure definitions and destroy them automatically after use, size them appropriately, tag resources by owner and purpose, and share expensive long-lived dependencies carefully. Cost should be visible to the team.

roles.codingRequirements: Scripting is expected: a language for test automation plus shell and cloud CLI usage. Infrastructure as code is usually read and occasionally modified, not authored from scratch.
commonMistakes: Assuming staging behaves like production without checking configuration parity
Testing only happy paths and ignoring partial failure of dependencies
Leaving test environments running and accumulating cost
Using over-privileged credentials for tests, which hides permission defects
readinessCriteria: Can deploy an application to a test environment and run automated tests against it
Has tested timeout, retry and failure behaviour of a dependency
Can verify least-privilege permissions with positive and negative tests
Has performed and measured a restore test

roles.title: Chaos Engineering Practitioner
roles.overview: A Chaos Engineering Practitioner runs controlled experiments that inject failures into systems to learn how they behave under turbulent conditions. They define steady-state hypotheses, limit blast radius, coordinate game days with operations teams and turn findings into resilience improvements.
responsibilities: Define steady-state metrics that represent normal system behaviour
Design experiments with a hypothesis, scope, abort conditions and rollback plan
Start in non-production environments and expand scope only with approval and safeguards
Facilitate game days with engineering and on-call teams
Inject failures such as instance termination, latency, dependency outages and resource exhaustion
Verify alerting, runbooks and incident response during experiments
Track findings to resolution and repeat experiments to confirm fixes

essential: Distributed systems failure modes
Observability: metrics, logs, traces and alerting
Experiment design with hypotheses and abort criteria
Strong communication and coordination
roleSpecific: Fault injection tooling
Blast radius control and safety mechanisms
Game day facilitation and post-experiment reviews
optional: Load testing to combine with fault injection
Site reliability engineering practices such as service level objectives

prerequisites: Experience with cloud or distributed systems

beginner.title: Principles and safe first experiments
goals: Explain the principles of chaos engineering and how it differs from random breakage
Write a steady-state hypothesis with measurable metrics
Terminate a container in a local environment and observe recovery
Define abort conditions for an experiment

intermediate.title: Structured experiments
goals: Inject latency into a dependency and verify timeouts and fallbacks
Run a game day in a staging environment with an on-call team
Verify alerts fire and runbooks are accurate during a failure
Document findings and action items in a blameless review

advanced.title: Resilience programme
goals: Plan a production experiment with minimal blast radius, approvals and automatic abort
Automate recurring experiments in a pipeline for regression
Prioritise experiments by risk and past incidents
Report resilience improvements over time

tools: A fault injection tool or framework
exercises: Write a full experiment plan for a dependency outage: hypothesis, metrics, scope, abort conditions, rollback and communication
In a local environment, inject 500 ms latency on a dependency and observe the effect on p95 latency and error rate
Design a game day agenda for a checkout service with roles and timeline
Turn three experiment findings into prioritised action items

sampleProject.title: Game day kit for a microservice demo
sampleProject.description: Run a small microservice application locally or in a cluster you control, with monitoring dashboards. Write three experiment plans (instance kill, dependency latency, database connection exhaustion), execute them with abort conditions, capture dashboards before and during each experiment, and write a blameless review with findings and follow-up actions.

interviewQuestions.q: What is a steady-state hypothesis?
interviewQuestions.a: A statement about measurable, normal system output that should hold during the experiment, for example 'checkout success rate stays above the agreed level and p99 latency stays under the target while one instance is terminated'. It focuses on user-visible outputs rather than internal details, and the experiment tries to disprove it.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you limit blast radius?
interviewQuestions.a: Start in non-production, then target the smallest scope in production: a single instance, a small share of traffic or internal users. Define automatic abort conditions tied to the steady-state metrics, have a tested rollback, run during staffed hours with stakeholders informed, and expand only after earlier experiments are understood.

interviewQuestions.q: Is chaos engineering just breaking things randomly?
interviewQuestions.a: No. It is disciplined experimentation: a hypothesis, controlled variables, minimal blast radius, monitoring and abort criteria, followed by analysis and fixes. Random breakage without observation or safeguards teaches little and causes avoidable incidents.

interviewQuestions.q: What happens after an experiment finds a weakness?
interviewQuestions.a: Stop or roll back if needed, document what happened against the hypothesis in a blameless review, create prioritised action items with owners, such as adding timeouts, fixing alerts or updating runbooks, and rerun the experiment after the fix to confirm the improvement.

interviewQuestions.q: When should you not run a chaos experiment?
interviewQuestions.a: When the system lacks the observability to see the effect, when there is no way to abort or roll back, during a live incident or peak business period, when known weaknesses have not been fixed (the outcome is already known), or without agreement from the owning teams.

roles.codingRequirements: Scripting and automation skills are needed for experiments and tooling, along with comfort with containers and infrastructure. Deep application development is not required.
commonMistakes: Running experiments without a hypothesis or monitoring, so nothing is learned
Starting in production with a large blast radius
Skipping the follow-up so findings never lead to fixes
Not informing on-call teams, causing confusion with a real incident
readinessCriteria: Can write a complete experiment plan with hypothesis, scope and abort criteria
Has executed at least two controlled experiments in a non-production environment
Has facilitated or participated in a game day and written a blameless review
Can explain how to expand experiments safely toward production
